risks.title: Procurement route near a printed boundary needs checking
risks.statement: Payments close to a published quotation boundary warrant checking the estimated total requirement and procurement route; proximity does not establish avoidance.

likelihood.justification: The general-procurement subset contains {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.tiers[3].by_tag.general_procurement.rows}} payments across {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.tiers[3].by_tag.general_procurement.suppliers}} suppliers [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.tiers[3].by_tag.general_procurement.rows] [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.tiers[3].by_tag.general_procurement.suppliers]. Likelihood is deliberately below the recurring-pattern baseline because payment proximity alone does not identify contract value or a missing quote [rule:CPR-70].

impact.justification: A missed quotation step could expose the Council to challenge, but neither a failed process nor serious consequence has been established. The provisional Minor descriptor reflects low possibility of legal challenge [history:IMPACT-2] [rule:CPR-70].

risks.proposed_focus: Check aggregation, contract category, VAT basis, quotations and any authorised exemption before judging the applicable route.
risks.prepared_control: The documented total requirement determines the quotation route and invitations are retained [rule:CPR-70] [rule:CPR-71].
risks.prepared_test: For each selected payment obtain the purchase order, requirement estimate and quotation file; establish contract category and total commitment, reconcile the VAT treatment, and inspect evidence of the applicable invitations or approved exemption. Do not treat payment value alone as contract value.
risks.prepared_evidence: Purchase orders, contract value estimates, quotation records, exemption approvals and VAT basis.
prepared_pbc: Requirement estimate and purchase order for each selected payment
Quotation invitations, evaluation records and any approved exemption
Documented resolution of the rulebook VAT and boundary ambiguities

risks.title: Related requirements may not have been aggregated
risks.statement: Recurring payments within the analytical window may represent related requirements that need an aggregation and procurement-route review.

likelihood.justification: The selected printed boundary has {{$.tests.split_purchases.tiers[1].headline.windows}} general-procurement windows across {{$.tests.split_purchases.tiers[1].by_tag.general_procurement.suppliers}} suppliers [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.tiers[1].headline.windows] [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.tiers[1].by_tag.general_procurement.suppliers]. This is a recurring-pattern planning indicator under the no-artificial-splitting rule; it is not evidence that these payments share a procurement requirement [rule:CPR-13].

impact.justification: If related requirements were improperly separated, lost competition or external criticism could fit the council’s provisional Medium compliance/reputation descriptors [history:IMPACT-3] [rule:CPR-13] [rule:CPR-70]. Flagged spend is not a loss estimate.

risks.proposed_focus: Confirm which payments belong to a single requirement, identify legitimate recurring or distinct services, then test aggregate value and route.
risks.prepared_control: Related requirements are assessed together and are not artificially split to avoid the applicable process [rule:CPR-13] [rule:CPR-70].
risks.prepared_test: Inspect the orders, service periods, requisitions and contract file for every selected window; determine whether the payments concern one requirement or separate legitimate needs, then compare documented aggregate value with the procurement route and approvals.
risks.prepared_evidence: Requisitions, orders, service descriptions, contract files, quote/tender evidence and approval records.
prepared_pbc: Requisitions and purchase orders for all payments in each sampled window
Service-period and requirement descriptions explaining recurrence
Contract, quotation or tender file and any waiver approval

risks.title: Repeated payment patterns require invoice validation
risks.statement: Equal-value payments to the same normalised supplier at different payment-run times may reflect legitimate recurring charges or duplicates; invoice-level reconciliation is required.

likelihood.justification: There are {{$.tests.duplicates.tiers.different_time.by_tag.general_procurement.rows}} general-procurement groups involving {{$.tests.duplicates.tiers.different_time.by_tag.general_procurement.suppliers}} suppliers in the different-time subset [metric:$.tests.duplicates.tiers.different_time.by_tag.general_procurement.rows] [metric:$.tests.duplicates.tiers.different_time.by_tag.general_procurement.suppliers]. Recurrence supports a planning review, while the Accounts Payable Reasonable Assurance opinion and absent invoice identifiers limit any conclusion [history:AUD-15].

impact.justification: Confirmed duplicate payments could require recovery and attract external criticism, consistent with a provisional Medium descriptor [history:IMPACT-3]. The amount after the first payment is only an indicator; valid and undisputed invoice terms remain the contractual reference [rule:CPR-44].

risks.proposed_focus: Compare invoice identifiers, service periods, credit notes and ledger records; keep same-timestamp batching separate from repeat payment runs.
risks.prepared_control: Contract payment terms relate to valid, undisputed invoices; sampled payments are reconciled to the underlying obligation before concluding that a repeat is a duplicate [rule:CPR-44] [rule:CPR-36].
risks.prepared_test: Reconcile every payment in each selected group to invoice number, service period, purchase order, contract payment terms and credits; classify distinct legitimate charges separately from any repeated settlement of the same obligation and request management explanation.
risks.prepared_evidence: Invoices, supplier ledger, credit notes, purchase orders, delivery or service confirmation and contract payment terms.
prepared_pbc: Underlying invoices and ledger entries for the sampled groups
Related credit notes and any recovery records
Contract payment terms and evidence supporting the billed service periods

risks.title: Published notice coverage needs reconciliation to the contract register
risks.statement: General-procurement suppliers above the printed publication boundary without an exact active notice match require contract-register reconciliation; missing notices do not establish off-contract spend.

likelihood.justification: The proxy reports {{$.tests.off_contract.headline.count}} general-procurement suppliers without an exact match [metric:$.tests.off_contract.headline.count]. Likelihood is reduced below the recurring-pattern baseline because public notices are incomplete and the Council contract register is not supplied [metric:$.contracts.register_present]. Near matches, legacy awards and lawful exemptions require review [rule:CPR-08] [history:AUD-01].

impact.justification: If award recording or contract documentation were missing, external scrutiny and a reasonable possibility of legal challenge could fit the provisional Medium descriptor [history:IMPACT-3] [rule:CPR-34]. The unmatched payment population is not evidence of such a failure or financial loss.

risks.proposed_focus: Obtain the actual register and contracts, confirm near matches, then identify awards and publication duties by category and date.
risks.prepared_control: All awards are notified for recording on the Council Contract Register and required contract information is published [rule:CPR-34] [rule:CPR-08].
risks.prepared_test: Reconcile each selected supplier and sampled payment to the Council register and signed contract; confirm any near-name match, legacy award, framework call-off or exemption, and inspect required award notification and publication evidence. Record unresolved coverage as an evidence gap.
risks.prepared_evidence: Council contract register, signed contracts, award notifications, framework call-off records and published notice identifiers.
prepared_pbc: Current Council contract register and award notifications
Signed contracts or call-off records for sampled payments
Explanation and supporting records for unmatched or near-matched suppliers

risks.title: Payments following published expiry need extension evidence
risks.statement: Payments after all exactly matched published notices have ended warrant checking whether a valid renewal, replacement or authorised extension covers the service.

likelihood.justification: The analysis identifies {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.count}} suppliers whose matched notices ended before the spend window [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.count]. The rating is below the recurring-pattern baseline because an unobserved newer contract may exist; approval remains an internal-record question [rule:CPR-77].

impact.justification: An unsupported extension could weaken contract enforceability or attract legal challenge; this is provisionally aligned to the Medium compliance descriptor [history:IMPACT-3] [rule:CPR-77]. Notice expiry itself does not establish an expired contract.

risks.proposed_focus: Inspect original extension clauses, the current contract and documented approval before treating notice dates as contractual expiry.
risks.prepared_control: A permitted contractual extension is supported by the required finance-officer approval [rule:CPR-77].
risks.prepared_test: For each selected supplier trace the payments to the current contract; inspect original extension rights, any replacement agreement and the recorded extension approval, distinguishing public-notice staleness from an unsupported extension.
risks.prepared_evidence: Original contract, extension clause, renewal or replacement agreement, approval record and payment linkage.
prepared_pbc: Current and predecessor contracts for the selected suppliers
Extension or renewal approvals and effective dates
Record linking sampled payments to the governing agreement

risks.title: Spend-to-award differences need scope and variation review
risks.statement: Annualised payment estimates above the annual rate implied by a matched award warrant reconciling scope, timing and any approved variation.

likelihood.justification: There are {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.count}} eligible supplier indicators [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.count]. Likelihood is reduced below the recurring-pattern baseline because annualisation, award estimates and multi-contract scope may explain the difference; this does not establish a variation [rule:CPR-78].

impact.justification: If a material change lacked the prescribed approval, it could raise a reasonable possibility of legal challenge under the Medium descriptor [history:IMPACT-3] [rule:CPR-78]. No estimate of contractual overspend or loss is asserted.

risks.proposed_focus: Reconcile payments to contract scope, duration and award value, then verify any modification and its required approval.
risks.prepared_control: Contract modifications are within the permitted scope and carry the approval required for the relevant value category [rule:CPR-78].
risks.prepared_test: Reconcile selected payments to the award scope and payment schedule; compare actual period expenditure with the contract basis rather than assuming annualisation proves overspend, and inspect change control, modification grounds and the applicable approval.
risks.prepared_evidence: Signed contract, award-value basis, invoices, payment schedule, change-control log and approval reports.
prepared_pbc: Award-value calculation, scope and payment schedule
Variation or change-control records with approvals
Explanation of timing or scope differences behind the annualised indicator

risks.title: Waiver and delegated-authority records require direct inspection
risks.statement: Public payment and notice data cannot establish whether exceptions were requested in advance, justified and approved by the correct delegated authority.

likelihood.justification: This is a rule-only governance gap without current evidence of failed approvals [rule:CPR-21] [rule:CPR-25] [rule:CPR-27]. Contract Letting previously received Reasonable Assurance and the supplied appendix contains no detailed finding to support an adverse uplift [history:AUD-01].

impact.justification: An unauthorised waiver could expose the procurement process to external criticism or legal challenge, provisionally matching the Medium descriptor [history:IMPACT-3] [rule:CPR-27]. Consequence information is not available.

risks.proposed_focus: Request the waiver register and delegation records, establish the population, and inspect advance timing, reasons and the relevant approval trail.

prepared_sample.note: Document/enquiry test; obtain the waiver population and authority records before selecting internal cases.

risks.prepared_control: Exceptions are sought in advance, documented and approved by the authorised roles; contract award authority follows the applicable delegation [rule:CPR-21] [rule:CPR-25] [rule:CPR-27] [rule:CPR-05].
risks.prepared_test: Obtain the waiver and exception population and current delegated-authority records; inspect documented reasons, timing, report approval and authorisation, referring unresolved threshold boundaries for human interpretation before reaching a compliance conclusion.
risks.prepared_evidence: Waiver register, exception reports, approval timestamps and delegated-authority records.
prepared_pbc: Waiver and exception register covering the payment period
Reports, reasons and dated authorisations for the selected internal cases
Applicable delegated-authority records and auditor-resolved statutory thresholds

risks.title: Placement exemptions need documented reasons for provider selection
risks.statement: Care and education placement payments need a separate review of exemption eligibility and documented provider-selection reasons; routine recurrence must not be treated as procurement splitting.

likelihood.justification: The population includes {{$.population.tags.care_or_education_placement.rows}} tagged placement payments [metric:$.population.tags.care_or_education_placement.rows], but tags do not prove exemption status or missing records. The case-note requirement is therefore rated as a rule-only gap [rule:CPR-79]. Residential and nursing care had Reasonable Assurance; the separate Direct Payments Limited Assurance opinion supplies no matching detailed finding, so no repeat uplift is applied [history:AUD-18] [history:AUD-16].

impact.justification: If provider-selection reasons were absent, the decision could attract external scrutiny consistent with the Medium reputation descriptor [history:IMPACT-3] [rule:CPR-79]. No deficient care, personal harm or financial loss is inferred.

risks.proposed_focus: Determine actual exemption category and inspect provider-selection reasons and applicable approval, with appropriate handling of personal information.

prepared_sample.note: Document/enquiry test; request a privacy-conscious case index and select internal records after confirming exemption category.

risks.prepared_control: Eligible individual placement arrangements retain the reasons for provider selection on the individual case notes [rule:CPR-79].
risks.prepared_test: Obtain an anonymised placement case index and establish which cases fall within the stated exemption; inspect the recorded reasons for provider selection and any applicable board approval without inferring a missing record from payment recurrence.
risks.prepared_evidence: Anonymised case index, exemption assessment, redacted provider-selection reasons and applicable approval records.
prepared_pbc: Anonymised placement case index and exemption categorisation
Redacted case-note evidence explaining provider selection
Applicable approval records without unnecessary personal information
